messages:
jen wang: Heads-up: premerge CI is failing on both SAST and our DAST smoke. Looks like a KMS decrypt error when the scanner tries to load test fixtures. CI link: https://ci.redwood.example/build/1234 :warning:
deploy-bot: build 1234 failed — exit code 1 — see logs: https://ci.redwood.example/build/1234/logs :robot_face:
matt p: curious — this only started after the keystore role change last night? @samir do you know if the ephemeral grant service was updated? :thinking_face:
samir: yep we rolled the keystore role change at 03:20 UTC. The ephemeral-grants service was bumped to v2.1.0 in the same deploy. I don't see explicit KMS errors in the deploy, but retry logic was tightened.
jen wang: logs show a 403 from KMS when scanner tries to decrypt testdata blob. snippet:
```
ERROR: failed to decrypt artifact: AccessDeniedException: Caller does not have permission to use the key
  at kms.Decrypt (keystore.go:178)
  at scanner.FetchFixture (scanner/fixtures.go:44)
```
alice: that 403 suggests either the service account lost kms:Decrypt or there is a key policy restriction. We should NOT bypass scans; need an evidence-preservation plan. :no_entry_sign:
matt p: for triage: can we reproduce locally with the service account token? I can try a quick repro and attach debug logs.
samir: repro locally shows same error when using the ephemeral token created by ephemeral-grants. The token looks valid but KMS logs show "principalMismatch" on the key policy.
jen wang: ok assign owner and next steps: 1) preserve CI artifacts (logs + failed fixtures) 2) collect KMS key policy snapshot 3) escalate to keystore owners for policy diff 4) decide rollback or ephemeral policy patch. Who takes 1 and 2? :clipboard:
alice: I can grab artifacts and upload to secure bucket. I'll add provenance metadata. Doing now.
security-bot: evidence ticket created: SEC-EVID-2026-89 — includes link to preserved artifacts.
matt p: I'll pull key policy via `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` and paste diff.
samir: I can produce the ephemeral-grants audit for the last deploy window (03:00–03:30 UTC). Will attach in thread.
jen wang: quick Q on scope: is this limited to the scanner path or do other consumers of the keystore fail? samir?
samir: quick smoke: other services that use long-lived service accounts are fine. Only consumers using ephemeral-grants tokens see the failure. Key policy change apparently added a condition requiring `request.auth.principal == serviceAccount:keystore@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` — ephemeral principals don't match.
alice: that's actionable then. Options: (A) relax key policy temporarily to allow ephemeral principal OR (B) have ephemeral-grants mint tokens that impersonate the keystore SA (needs IAM binding + approval).
matt p: option B is cleaner long-term, but needs a few reviewers. For immediate unblocking we might need an emergency policy patch with audit trail. Can we do a short-lived grant?
jen wang: agree. Per incident playbook: emergency keystore policy change must have 2 approvers from security and platform and must be logged. @samir can you propose a minimal policy patch (time-bound) and I'll route approvals?
samir: propose patch: allow `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` for principal `serviceAccount:ephemeral-grants@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` but with `condition` restricting `request.time < "2026-03-21T06:00:00Z"` and `request.resource.name` matches project key path. I'll paste JSON in a sec.
jen wang: pinging @alice and @matt for approvals. Also we need to file an incident record if we change policy. Who will draft the incident summary?
alice: I'll draft the incident summary and timeline using preserved artifacts.
matt p: I approve the temporary policy change (for emergency unblock). :+1:
alice: I approve as well after I see the exact JSON. :eyes:
samir: policy patch JSON:
```json
{"bindings": [{"role":"roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter","members":["serviceAccount:ephemeral-grants@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"],"condition":{"title":"temp-scan-unblock","description":"temporary unblock for scanner CI","expression":"request.time < timestamp(\"2026-03-21T06:00:00Z\")"}}]}
```
jen wang: tagging compliance: we will need a postmortem and evidence of who approved and when. I'll create postmortem stub in the incident tracker and link SEC-EVID-2026-89.
security-bot: incident record created: SEC-INC-2026-23 — responders: jen wang, alice, matt p, samir.
deploy-bot: policy patch applied by samir at 04:05 UTC (audit-id: a1b2c3). CI retriggered.
matt p: CI retrigger shows scanners passing now. build 1235 green: https://ci.redwood.example/build/1235 :rocket:
jen wang: great — keep this thread as the canonical evidence chain. Follow-ups: 1) permanent fix: make ephemeral-grants impersonate keystore SA or adjust key policy with stable principal mapping 2) add a preflight check in CI that validates keystore access before scan step 3) update deploy checklist to highlight key-policy diffs.
alice: adding tasks to SEC backlog and will assign owners.
samir: I'll open PR on ephemeral-grants to support impersonation flow and include unit tests for KMS decrypt path.
jen wang: thanks all. Closing action: alice will attach final postmortem and link SEC-INC-2026-23.
summary: Premerge SAST + DAST blocked by KMS key policy change affecting ephemeral tokens; emergency temporary key policy patch applied after approvals; artifacts preserved and incident created for postmortem.
